subject: Greenfield Health — isolation model clarifications and artifact request
messages:

Cc: security-eval@greenfieldhealth.com

Subject: Greenfield Health security questionnaire — tenant isolation artefacts request

Hi Mina / Marcus,

Thanks for the quick intro on the RFP. As part of our security review we need a concise set of artefacts and short clarifications related to your isolation model so we can sign off on the next phase. Can you provide the following by EOD Wednesday (your timezone)?

1) A network/topology diagram that shows Tenant boundaries, control plane vs data plane, and where sidecars/KV caches live (file format: SVG or PNG).
2) One-page threat model summary describing the primary attack surfaces you consider for multi-tenant inference (esp. lateral movement and KV cache leakage).
3) A short description of egress controls (NAT, proxies, per-tenant NAT vs shared egress) and how you perform outbound filtering.
4) Evidence of audit logging for keys and model load events (where retained, how long, and how a customer can request logs).
5) Anything you can share regarding private deployment options (VPC, on-prem) and how isolation is enforced there.

If you have a checklist or CSV mapping of controls to evidence, that would be very helpful. We may follow up with targeted clarifying questions.

Thanks — Olivia
Olivia Grant
Security Evaluation Lead
Greenfield Health

Subject: Re: Greenfield Health security questionnaire — tenant isolation artefacts request

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear list. Attaching the two primary artefacts you requested and a short summary below. If anything is missing we can hop on a 30-min call and walk through the diagram.

Attachments: gfh_requested_isolation_diagram.svg (SVG), gfh_threat_model_summary.pdf (PDF)

Quick answers (overview):
- Topology: Each tenant runs isolated inference workers in per-tenant compute pools. Control plane (orchestration, rollout) is on a separate management network and never directly accessible from tenant data plane. The attached SVG highlights the tenant boundary, sidecar placement, and network ACLs at the subnet level.
- KV cache and sidecars: KV caches are per-tenant by default and run inside the tenant slice; sidecar proxies mediate all outgoing model artifact fetches and inter-node RPCs. There is an optional shared read-only cache for public models (not used for private customer model payloads).
- Egress model: We operate per-region egress gateways with per-tenant NAT translation where required. Outbound flows leave through managed egress proxies that perform TLS inspection at customer request and route via customer peering or our managed NAT. Details in the diagram and the attached threat summary.
- Audit logs & retention: Key events (KMS operations, model loads, rollout events) are recorded to an append-only audit stream and retained as part of the customer's evidence package for 365 days by default; retention can be extended under enterprise contract. We include indices for quick retrieval.
- Private deployment: Private control plane + customer-managed VPC is supported. Isolation is enforced via dedicated VPC routing policies, subnets, and network policies; documented in the last section of the threat summary.

Next steps: review the attachments and tell us any gaps you want filled or whether you'd like a walkthrough.

Best,

Mina Haddad
Security & Compliance Lead
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-03-15T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Greenfield Health security questionnaire — tenant isolation artefacts request

Olivia / Mina — adding a couple of technical clarifications to avoid ambiguity in the diagram and threat summary. I've attached a small CSV (redwood_egress_controls_table.csv) mapping controls to evidence artifacts.

Key points:
- L3 isolation: Tenants are placed into logically separate subnets and enforced via VPC route tables and security groups. Inter-tenant traffic is blocked by default; all inter-node RPCs are authenticated via mTLS between per-tenant identities.

- Sidecar behavior (short): sidecars terminate TLS from the application, enforce request-level ACLs, and hold per-tenant ephemeral credentials to fetch model files from the object store. Sidecars drop request headers that could leak tenant provenance to shared services.

- KV caches: Each tenant's KV cache instances run with distinct encryption keys (KMS key per-tenant) and are mounted in isolated namespaces. Eviction and cold-start policies are designed to prevent cross-tenant data persistence.

- NAT/egress: We support both per-tenant NAT (recommended for stricter audit) and shared NAT with source-IP tagging. Egress filtering is done at our managed proxy tier; customers can provide allowlists or route egress via their peering for full isolation.

Attachment referenced: redwood_egress_controls_table.csv — mapping of control -> evidence (diagram page / log sample / KMS artifact).

Let us know if you want sample log extracts (sanitized) or a retention SLA statement.

Thanks,
Marcus
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Thanks — the artefacts look good at a glance. A couple of clarifying questions before we move to our internal review:

1) For the per-tenant KMS keys you mentioned, are keys always customer-controlled in Private deployments or are there modes where Redwood retains key custody? Please indicate default and enterprise-behavior.
2) Can you confirm whether sidecars ever access shared object storage endpoints for model materialization (we're trying to understand any cross-tenant attack surface while model files are pulled).
3) Do you provide a sample of the audit log format for model-load events (timestamp, model-id, tenant-id, node-id, triggered-by) or a sanitized example we can ingest into our tooling?

We'd like to schedule a short 30-minute call next week with your architecture team to walk the diagram (Tue/Wed morning PT preferred). Also attaching our internal checklist for your reference: GNH-security-checklist.xlsx

Regards,
Olivia

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Greenfield Health security questionnaire — tenant isolation artefacts request

Hi Olivia — answers inline below and next steps.

1) KMS custody: By default (hosted offering) Redwood manages the KMS keys with strict access controls and audit trails; for Private deployments we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) in which the customer retains custody and we never have the key material. This is documented in our control matrix and can be contractually required for regulated workloads.

2) Model materialization: Sidecars fetch model artifacts from object storage over mTLS authenticated channels. In hosted/private configurations for dedicated/private model payloads the storage path is tenant-scoped and uses per-tenant encryption keys. Shared public-model caches exist but they are read-only and never used to materialize tenant-private model blobs. The diagram page 2 (in the SVG) highlights this flow.

3) Audit log sample: Yes — we can provide a sanitized sample CSV showing fields: event_ts, event_type, model_id, tenant_id, node_id, request_id, actor. If that format works we will upload a sanitized example to the Drive link I included. Retention: default 365 days; extended retention available via contract.

Scheduling: Tue 2027-03-22 09:00 PT works for our architecture team. I'll send a calendar invite once you confirm.

Evidence we attached (again): gfh_requested_isolation_diagram.svg, gfh_threat_model_summary.pdf, redwood_egress_controls_table.csv. Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cGFH-security-evidence
